overall: The AG found the Nahant Housing Authority violated the Open Meeting Law by holding its January 7, 2014 meeting in a location not accessible to all members of the public; the notice-posting and agenda-participation allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 7, 2014 meeting was held in a location that did not comply with the ADA, limiting access for people with disabilities.
allegations.key_passage: The Authority violated the Open Meeting Law because the location for its January 7, 2014 meeting was not ADA compliant, thereby impeding the public's access to the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Authority failed to post notice of the January 7, 2014 meeting in the lobby of the building where it meets.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Authority complied with the Open Meeting Law's requirements by posting notice of its January 7, 2014 meeting on the bulletin board outside of Town Hall, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Authority declined her requests to be placed on the December 3, 2013 and January 7, 2014 agendas to participate in those meetings.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Authority did not violate the Open Meeting Law by declining the complainant's requests to be added to certain meeting agendas.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
